messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Re: how fast when poppr by a 10k or more snps
parts:
Hi,

I'm afraid this is still vague as I don't know anything about your system (how much memory you have or what versions of software you are running).

My only explanation is that you are calculating the index of association over a vast number of SNPs. At one point during this calculation, your computer must compute over 3 billion values, which alone would take ~3GiB on your computer. You might consider using genlight objects as a more efficient storage mode for your data as we have optimized procedures (e.g. bitwise.ia) for dealing with large numbers of SNPs in genlight format.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

I would suggest for you to use the vcfR package to read in your VCF file and then export it to a snpclone object:

https://knausb.github.io/vcfR_documentation/export_genlight_snpclone.html

From there, you can use diversity_table() to calculate genotypic diversity and win.ia(), sample.ia() or bitwise.ia() to calculate the index of association.

Hope that helps,
Zhian
